Ishmael Reed's Japanese by Spring is a multilingual and multicultural novel which is a critique of the racial and cultural politics of the United States.
the novel is an attempt to show how the desire for linguistic capital is racialized, and how the racialization of the desire for linguistic power is a result of the racialization of language.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Japanese By Spring offers a nuanced understanding of multilingualism as an alternative to the racialization of language that undergirds the multiculturalism in the US.
the novel shows the ways in which linguistic capital, like cultural capital, is a form of social capital that is unequally distributed in a racially stratified society.
we have found that Japanese By Spring is a novel about language, race and the politics of identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

multilingualism, as a form of capital, is not a panacea for the problems of multiculturalism, as the latter is not merely an effect of linguistic pluralism, but is also shaped by the social, economic, and political conditions that produce the racialized subjects that populate it.
the novel’s protagonist, who is a black American, is unable to attain the status of a “true” American because he cannot access the linguistic capital that would enable him to do so.

the novel is not only a critique of multiculturalism, but also a caution against the tendency to see language as a matter of voluntary association, which is the premise of the approach that sees language as a corrective to race.
